battle.name: 達魯古城之戰
battle.brief: 達魯古城之戰是1115年在安納托利亞達魯古城爆發的戰役，屬中世紀安納托利亞邊境的一次軍事衝突。達魯古城位於安納托利亞中部，扼守內陸交通，成為交戰各方關注的城市。拜占庭方面配置配重投石車（Trebuchet，1100年），用於圍城遠程打擊，攻擊城牆與城門，並與其他攻城器械協同部署。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 達魯古城之戰是公元1115年遼西邊地的一場野戰，交戰一方是女真完顏部建立的早期金政權，另一方是契丹人建立的遼朝。戰場為達魯古城，位於今內蒙古東部的遼西邊地，較常見的定位落在赤峰、通遼一帶。戰役通常列於金收國元年、遼天慶四年，時間多置於1115年年初；傳本紀年與公曆換算略有歧義，故本篇不虛指某一日。地理上，達魯連接遼東平原、女真聚居地與蒙古高原東南部，是遼朝防線向西北延伸的節點。金軍由女真根據地經已奪取的寧宏等據點向西推進，遼軍則從遼朝腹地調集兵力，向達魯方向進逼。交戰重心在城外曠野，並非其後金軍進攻遼朝五京時的攻城戰。
countriesEn: The Battle of Dalu was a field engagement fought in the western frontier region of Liao in 1115. One belligerent was the early Jin polity established by the Jurchen Wanyan clan, while the other was the Khitan-founded Liao dynasty. The battlefield was Dalu, an ancient city in the eastern part of present-day Inner Mongolia, generally placed in the broader area between Chifeng and Tongliao. The campaign is usually assigned to the first year of Jin's Shouguo era and the fourth year of Liao's Tianqing era, and is generally placed near the beginning of 1115. Because the transmitted chronologies and their conversion to the Gregorian calendar differ slightly, no exact day is asserted here. Geographically, Dalu connected the Liaodong plain, the Jurchen homeland, and the southeastern Mongolian plateau, forming a node in Liao's frontier system extending toward the northwest. The Jin force advanced westward from the Jurchen base through places such as Ningfu, which it had already seized, while Liao assembled troops from the interior of the dynasty and moved toward Dalu. The main fighting occurred on open ground outside the city rather than in the later siege warfare against Liao's five capitals.
people: 此役的核心人物是完顏阿骨打。他以女真完顏部首領的身分集結武力，主動奪取寧宏等據點，再把兵力壓向達魯；他親自統兵並在城外接戰，因此不是只坐鎮後方的抽象主帥。遼方統兵者為高儼，率領遼朝調來的野戰大軍；遼天祚帝耶律宗真並未到陣前，軍令由中樞下達，較長的傳令距離與複雜的指揮鏈，使遼軍各部難以同時協同。《金史》把完顏宗翰等女真將領列入早期攻遼的從征記錄，卻沒有保存達魯城外各部的確切站位、傳令次序或個人斬獲，因此不能把後來金史中的封賞細節倒填到此役，也沒有可靠依據為阿骨打或高儼添加陣前對白。兩人的實際作用分別是率領金軍完成攻勢，以及主持最終被切斷的遼軍指揮核心。
peopleEn: The central figure was Wanyan Aguda. As leader of the Jurchen Wanyan clan, he gathered forces, took places such as Ningfu, and then pressed toward Dalu. He personally commanded the troops in the engagement outside the city and was therefore more than an abstract commander remaining safely in the rear. Gao Yan commanded the Liao field army sent by the dynasty. Liao's Tianzuo Emperor, Yelü Zong, was not present at the battlefield; orders came from the central government, and the long command distances and complicated chain of command made simultaneous coordination among Liao's formations difficult. The History of Jin records Wanyan Zonghan and other Jurchen commanders among the participants in the early campaigns against Liao, but it does not preserve their exact positions before Dalu, the sequence of messages, or individual tallies. Later honors recorded in the History of Jin therefore cannot be projected backward into this battle, and there is no sound basis for adding spoken exchanges between Aguda and Gao Yan. Their respective roles were to lead the Jin offensive and to head the Liao command structure that was ultimately broken.
kits: 雙方使用的裝備都可在1115年以前找到實物或文獻依據。金軍以女真地區早已使用的角弓為主要弓種，配備骨鏃、石鏃、鐵鏃箭矢及鳴鏑箭；近戰則有長槍、環首刀、斧與骨朵，護具包括皮甲、札甲和鐵質兜鍪。遼軍可見弓、弩、長槍、刀、斧、魚鱗甲、札甲與皮甲，騎兵另有箭囊、弓袋、鞍具、韁繩和馬鐙。角弓、札甲、魚鱗甲、鳴鏑箭與弩均早於此役，沒有戰後才出現的幻想兵器；交戰記錄中亦未出現火器或爆炸性武器。箭矢存量、各級軍人的護甲比例和每名射手攜帶數量都沒有留下數字。遼軍兵額龐大，後方須照顧糧秣、飲水、 fodder、輜重與替換馬匹，行列負擔較重；金軍規模較小，補給形式較便於集中與轉移，但同樣需要便攜食物、水與馬匹維修條件，兩軍都無法只靠一次突擊便持續作戰。
kitsEn: Both sides used equipment that is documented in texts or surviving examples from 1115 or earlier. The Jin drew its principal bow from the horn-backed composite bow long used in the Jurchen region, together with bone, stone, and iron arrowheads and whistling arrows. Close combat equipment included long spears, ring-pommel swords, axes, and bone-headed maces, while protection included leather armor, lamellar armor, and iron helmets. Liao forces could use bows, crossbows, spears, swords, axes, fish-scale armor, lamellar armor, and leather armor. Their mounted troops also carried arrow cases, bow cases, saddles, bridles, and stirrups. The horn bow, lamellar armor, fish-scale armor, whistling arrow, and crossbow all predate the campaign, and no retrospective or imaginary weapon appears in it. The records contain no firepower or explosive weapon in the fighting. No figures survive for ammunition stocks, armor coverage by rank, or the number of arrows carried by each archer. The much larger Liao host had to support provisions, water, fodder, baggage, and remounts, making its rear columns heavier. The smaller Jin force could concentrate and shift more easily, but it also required portable food, water, and means of maintaining horses. Neither army could remain in combat indefinitely from one sudden charge alone.
tactics: 接戰前，金軍已利用早期攻勢控制寧宏等據點，主動把達魯推到前線；金軍沒有把全部兵力耗在攻城上，而是在城外選地等候遼軍展開。阿骨打所部規模較小，維持緊密的部族小隊，不把全線拉得與遼軍一樣寬；前段以角弓和箭矢射擊遼軍前鋒，騎兵利用中軍與翼側的移動尋找缺口，待前線受壓而縱深調度不及，再集中本部骨幹突入，近距離再由槍、刀、斧和角弓完成纏鬥。這是依《金史》保存的勝負、兵種配置與遼軍潰散次序所作的有限重建，並非逐條命令的原文。遼軍前部一旦被切斷，後隊擠入缺口，通往營帳和輜重的退路迅速堵塞；金軍由攻擊受挫的前鋒轉為追擊潰兵，部分本紀把戰線延伸至阿術岡一帶。達魯城本身不是全日強攻的焦點，主要成果是野外解除遼軍增援並打斷其指揮。關於是否有固定詐敗、預埋伏兵或某一刻風沙決定勝局，傳本說法不足以互證，本文不把二手細節當作事實。
tacticsEn: Before contact, the Jin had used its early offensive to seize places such as Ningfu and had carried the struggle forward to Dalu. Rather than exhausting the entire force in an assault on the walls, the Jin selected ground outside the city and waited for the Liao army to deploy. Aguda's force was comparatively small and retained compact clan formations instead of spreading its front to the same width as the Liao line. In the initial phase, horn bows and arrows engaged the Liao vanguard, while mounted troops looked for openings between the center and the flanks. Once pressure on the front was followed by inadequate movement in the Liao depth, the Jin concentrated its clan core in the breach; at close range, spears, swords, axes, and bows completed the fighting. This is a limited reconstruction based on the preserved outcome, force configuration, and sequence of the Liao collapse, not a verbatim copy of individual orders. Once the Liao front was cut, later formations crowded into the gap and blocked the routes back to the tents and baggage. The Jin then shifted from striking the resistant forward units to pursuing the routed. Some dynastic annals extend the pursuit to the area of Ashugang. Dalu itself was not the focus of an all-day storm; the main result was the defeat of the field relief army and the disruption of Liao command in the open country. The transmitted accounts do not provide mutually consistent proof of a set feigned retreat, a prepared ambush, or a single decisive gust of wind and dust, so such details from later retellings are not presented as established fact.
data: 可核對的數字主要來自後出的《金史》及《遼史》相關記載，而不是戰前點名冊。常見說法以二千五百人指阿骨打最初集結的核心武裝，以七萬指高儼所領遼軍；前者不是達魯交戰時金軍的確定總數，後者也不宜當作逐一核驗的headcount，金軍在起義初期吸收的歸附者、各部人數與戰前新增兵力均未被完整記載。戰役沒有留下可獨立核驗的首級、俘獲、重傷與逃亡總數，後世把七萬軍額直接寫成七萬死傷的算法也不能成立。達魯及阿術岡可定位在戰線上，但距離寧宏有多遠、每日行軍多少、箭矢存量、從何處补水以及糧秣由多少車輛承載，現有史料都未留下明細。日期方面，通常編為1115年年初，遼紀年為天慶四年、金紀年為收國元年；各本換算略有差異，故較可靠的是年份、交戰先後與勝負，而非一個過度精確的公曆日。
dataEn: The figures that can be compared come mainly from the later History of Jin and relevant passages in the History of Liao rather than from a contemporary roster. A commonly repeated account gives 2,500 for the core armed force Aguda first assembled and 70,000 for Gao Yan's Liao army. The first number is not a secure total for the Jin force at Dalu, and the second should not be treated as a verified headcount. The numbers of Jurchen followers absorbed during the early revolt, the strength of individual clans, and the troops added before the battle were not fully recorded. No independently verifiable totals survive for enemy dead, prisoners, severely wounded, or fugitives, and later equations of the reported army size with the same number of casualties are not historically valid. Dalu and Ashugang can be placed along the course of the fighting, but the records give no exact distance from Ningfu, daily rate of march, ammunition reserve, watering points, or number of vehicles carrying provisions. The engagement is usually placed near the beginning of 1115, in the fourth year of Liao's Tianqing era and the first year of Jin's Shouguo era. Since the converted dates differ among editions, the year, general sequence, and result are more secure than an artificially precise Gregorian day.
cause: 達魯之戰的近因，是遼朝調集重兵壓制已經開始的女真武裝起義。遼朝對女真各部長期徵取貢賦、稅役與使役，並以使節、拘押及軍事部署限制部首，女真各部對這種統治的不滿逐步加深；完顏阿骨打聚集本部的人手、馬匹和弓箭後，攻擊遼方官署與據點，起義由氏族衝突轉為公開戰爭。阿骨打沒有能力立即攻滅整個遼朝，因此初期目標是奪取邊城、取得裝備並擴大支持者；遼廷則企圖在高儼所領大軍仍完整時摧毀金軍的軍事核心，阻止更多女真部眾加入。達魯因而成為遼軍必須救援的邊防節點，也成為兩軍首次大規模野外決戰的場所。這不是缺乏政治背景的偶發遭遇戰：近因是遼軍的鎮壓，較深原因是邊疆徵斂、權力控制與女真部族自衛需求之間的衝突，而地理上則是達魯一線的攻防。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the Battle of Dalu was the movement of a major Liao army to suppress an armed Jurchen revolt that had already begun. Liao had long drawn tribute, taxes, labor, and other exactions from the Jurchen communities and limited their chiefs through envoys, detention, and military deployments. Resentment toward this rule accumulated across the Jurchen clans. After Wanyan Aguda had gathered men, horses, and bows from his own clan, attacks on Liao officials and garrisons turned a tribal conflict into open war. Aguda lacked the means to destroy the entire Liao dynasty immediately, so his early objectives were to seize frontier settlements, obtain equipment, and attract additional supporters. The Liao court, in turn, sought to destroy the emerging Jin military center while Gao Yan's army remained intact, thereby preventing further Jurchen participation. Dalu consequently became a frontier position that required relief and the site of the first major open-field decision between the two forces. The battle was not an accidental clash without political background: its immediate cause was Liao's attempt to suppress the revolt, its deeper cause lay in fiscal extraction, political control, and the Jurchen clans' need to defend themselves, and its geographical cause was the struggle over the Dalu corridor.
impact: 達魯的野外勝利首先改變了遼西邊地的力量平衡。遼軍的野戰指揮被打斷，後方供應與前線之間的通路短暫失去保障；金軍則取得一批甲械、武器、馬匹及其他軍用物資，能以更低成本繼續擴充騎兵和射手。完顏阿骨打的軍事聲望與女真各部對他的支持隨之上升，使1115年正式以金為號的建號過程獲得重要軍事支柱。遼朝沒有因達魯一役立即崩潰，仍保有五京與中央政權，並重新集結兵馬；金軍後來對遼朝堅固城邑的攻勢也曾受挫，顯示一次野戰勝利不會自動轉化為攻城能力。1122年遼朝才在持續戰爭中覆亡，因此達魯之戰應被視為金軍取得戰略主動權的關鍵起點，而不是足以單獨解釋遼亡的單一原因。它帶來了資源、士氣與建號的條件，也迫使遼廷把注意力集中於北方邊軍。
impactEn: The field victory at Dalu immediately altered the balance of power on Liao's western frontier. Liao's field command was broken, and the connection between its rear supply system and the forward army was temporarily disrupted. The Jin acquired armor, weapons, horses, and other military resources that allowed it to expand its mounted and missile forces at lower cost. Aguda's military reputation rose, as did support for him among additional Jurchen clans. This gave the formal establishment of the Jin name in 1115 an important military foundation. Liao did not collapse immediately after Dalu; it retained its five capitals and central government and assembled fresh forces. Jin's later attacks on strongly fortified Liao positions also encountered setbacks, showing that an open-field victory did not automatically become siege capability. Liao finally fell in 1122 after years of continuing war, so Dalu is best understood as the point at which the Jin gained strategic initiative rather than as a single cause sufficient to explain Liao's destruction. The battle supplied resources, prestige, and practical support for the new dynasty, while forcing the Liao court to concentrate its attention on the northern frontier army.
result: 達魯之戰的最終operational結果相當明確：高儼所領遼軍在城外失去原有的指揮與陣形，潰兵不能重新編組，遼軍對達魯方向的增援失敗；金軍控制戰場，並把達魯一帶的邊防通道轉入自己掌握，取得裝備與馬匹後得以繼續向西、向南擴張。史料不能支持把遼軍七萬全部寫成死亡或俘虜，也沒有留下可互證的雙方精確傷亡總數。高儼本人是否在戰場當場被擒，所見傳本記載不一，因此較可靠的結論只到其指揮核心被擊潰為止。達魯之役也不是遼朝的立即滅亡；遼廷仍能重組軍隊並繼續抵抗，直至1122年才失去主要政權。就戰役本身而言，結束於金軍掌握戰場、遼軍增援瓦解，以及兩軍隨後分別轉入鞏固達魯與重整防線的狀態。
resultEn: The operational outcome of the Battle of Dalu is clear: Gao Yan's Liao army lost its coherent command and formation in the field outside the city, the routed troops could not be reorganized effectively, and the Liao relief effort toward Dalu failed. The Jin gained control of the battlefield and took possession of the frontier corridor around Dalu, then used captured equipment and horses to support further expansion toward the west and south. The records do not support converting the reported figure of 70,000 Liao troops into 70,000 dead or captured men, and no mutually verifiable exact casualty total survives for either side. The transmitted accounts do not agree consistently on whether Gao Yan was captured at the battlefield itself, so the secure conclusion ends with the destruction of his command structure rather than a definite personal fate. Dalu did not produce the immediate destruction of Liao; the court was still able to rebuild an army and continue resistance, and the dynasty did not lose its principal political centers until 1122. The battle itself ended with Jin possession of the field, the collapse of the Liao relief force, and the two sides then moving respectively toward consolidation at Dalu and the restoration of Liao's defensive arrangements.
